note: GOVERNANCE FOUNDATION ONLY. This document establishes the phase, its requirements, and the binding execution security contract. Nothing in this phase is implemented or verified: every requirement below carries implementation.state NOT_STARTED and verification.state NOT_STARTED, and the Task Runner does not exist. The User's authorization of 2026-10-10 (recorded in sps2/decisions/P17-DECISIONS.json as D-P17-APPROVAL) approves the governance foundation only. Task Runner implementation is prohibited until GATE-P17-2 passes, and no real task may execute until GATE-P17-3 passes. No agent CLI was executed to produce this document.
roadmap_objective: Accept a task, prepare an ordered plan, discover authorized agents at runtime, select one deterministically with recorded rationale, execute locally under a controlled security contract, verify the result independently, and preserve auditable evidence.
roadmap_forbidden: public deployment; public network exposure; unrestricted autonomous execution; invoking any CLI outside the explicit authorized allowlist; circumventing provider limits, account restrictions, or terms; automatic account rotation intended to bypass quotas; exposing credentials in plans, logs, transcripts, or evidence; bypassing existing approval gates; installing dependencies
roadmap_deliverables: task-record schema (sps2/schemas/p17-task-record.schema.json); execution security contract; Task Runner implementation (only after GATE-P17-2); negative security suite; per-task evidence records
roadmap_acceptance: a real task executes end-to-end with a recorded ordered plan, runtime agent discovery, deterministic selection with rationale, bounded and captured execution, independent objective verification, and a complete evidence record; every failure mode (missing authorization, invalid task input, unavailable agent, timeout, execution failure, failed acceptance) produces an explicit auditable outcome
roadmap_verification: end-to-end demonstration with captured evidence plus the negative security suite (timeout kill, confinement violation attempt, secret-scrubbing, fail-closed paths, allowlist enforcement)
roadmap_rollback: remove the Task Runner; the governance foundation, schemas, and decision records remain additive and inert

standing_bounds.three_axis_rule: IMPLEMENTED != VERIFIED != APPROVED (sps2/core/SPEC.md; .sps/GOVERNANCE.md §1-§2). No artifact of this phase may collapse the three axes.
standing_bounds.P8/P9: APPROVED and must not be modified by P17 work
standing_bounds.P10: APPROVED requirements/schema only (D-P10-APPROVAL); P10 inventory population remains blocked on UQ-P10-05 and is untouched by this phase
standing_bounds.CONF-001: UNRESOLVED - no LCP or INP numeric threshold may appear in any P17 artifact
standing_bounds.stack_constraint: Python standard library only; project-local; no dependency installation (REQ-P17-12)
standing_bounds.security_boundary: Local-only execution. No public server, no public network exposure, no deployment (REQ-P17-05, SEC-P17-01)

dependency_state.P3: COMPLETE - adapter registry present (sps2/core/adapters/); adapters are declarative capability descriptors and define no invocation contract; P17 must not rely on them for execution semantics

requirements.title: Task intake
requirements.objective: Accept a task from a local interface (CLI argument or task file) with a unique task identifier, goal, required capabilities, and an objective acceptance command; reject malformed input fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: A task record conforming to sps2.p17-task-record/v1 is created with a unique TASK-P17-NNNN identifier before any work begins
Malformed or incomplete task input is rejected with an explicit error and a non-zero exit; no partial record is created
Task input containing credential-like material is rejected, not stored
security_implications: Intake is the trust boundary: invalid input must never reach plan generation or execution

requirements.title: Ordered plan generation
requirements.objective: Decompose an accepted task into an ordered plan of steps, persist it to project-local state, and gate execution on explicit approval of the plan (plan-first, zero-execution-before-approval).
acceptance_criteria: Every task carries an ordered plan with at least one step before execution
The plan is persisted to project-local state (.sps/tasks/) and is human-readable
Execution does not begin until the plan is approved, and the approval is recorded in the task record
Each plan step names its required agent capabilities so selection can be deterministic
security_implications: The plan gate is the primary control against autonomous execution; an unapproved plan must never execute

requirements.title: Runtime agent discovery
requirements.objective: Discover which authorized CLI agents are available at runtime by probing an explicit allowlist; never assume availability from documentation, configuration, or prior runs.
acceptance_criteria: Availability is determined by an executed runtime probe (executable present on PATH and responsive to a version or help invocation), not by documentation or configuration claims
The discovery snapshot (agent id, availability, version, probe method, probed-at timestamp) is recorded in the task record
An agent documented in the repository but absent at runtime is reported unavailable and is never selected
Discovery fails closed with an explicit auditable outcome when no authorized agent is available
security_implications: Assuming availability is how unreviewed or absent tooling silently enters the execution path

requirements.title: Deterministic agent selection
requirements.objective: Select an agent deterministically from the discovery snapshot against the task's required capabilities, with a recorded rationale and a reproducible selection fingerprint.
acceptance_criteria: The same requirement and discovery snapshot always yield the same selected agent and the same selection fingerprint
The selection rationale records why the selected agent was chosen and why the alternatives were not
Selection never falls back to an agent outside the authorized allowlist
When no available agent satisfies the required capabilities, selection is an explicit auditable failure, never an arbitrary choice
security_implications: Non-deterministic selection is an unauditable choice of executor; determinism is the control

requirements.title: Controlled local subprocess execution
requirements.objective: Execute the selected agent as a local subprocess under a bounded timeout with captured stdout/stderr, a recorded exit status, and an auditable execution record; the harness itself creates no network exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Every execution has an explicit bounded timeout; a timed-out process is terminated and recorded with outcome TIMEOUT
stdout and stderr are captured to transcript files referenced by path and SHA-256 digest in the task record
The exit status is recorded verbatim; a non-zero exit is an explicit auditable outcome, never silently treated as success
The harness opens no listening socket and makes no network request of its own; it only spawns the authorized local CLI
security_implications: Unbounded execution and lost output are how runaway or destructive agent behaviour becomes undetectable

requirements.title: Directory confinement
requirements.objective: Restrict every execution to the authorized project boundary using a tested containment mechanism, not merely a working-directory setting.
acceptance_criteria: The containment mechanism is defined in the implementation and covered by a negative test that attempts to write outside the project boundary and fails closed
The working directory alone is never the only containment control
A confinement violation produces an explicit auditable failure and no partial state outside the boundary
security_implications: A working-directory setting is a convention, not a boundary; containment must be enforced and tested

requirements.title: Credential safety
requirements.objective: Never expose API keys, environment secrets, or credentials in task plans, logs, transcripts, or evidence; grant no unrestricted credential access.
acceptance_criteria: Task records, plans, transcripts, and evidence contain no secret values; secrets are referenced by location only (.sps/GOVERNANCE.md §7)
The execution environment is constructed with an explicit, minimal policy; inherited secrets are not passed through by default
A credential-scrubbing check is part of the negative suite and fails when a secret pattern appears in any recorded artefact
security_implications: A single leaked credential in a transcript is a permanent disclosure; scrubbing is a control, not a cleanup

requirements.title: Independent objective verification
requirements.objective: Verify task results independently of the executing agent: a successful agent exit code or the agent's own claim is never proof that the task passed.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance is judged by an objective acceptance command or an independent verifier structurally separate from the executor
The verification result (PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED) with its evidence reference is recorded in the task record
A task whose acceptance command fails is recorded as failed with a non-zero overall outcome, even if the agent exited 0
The verifier's independence from the executor is stated in the task record
security_implications: Executor self-attestation is the exact failure mode the three-axis rule exists to prevent

requirements.title: Fail-closed behavior
requirements.objective: Missing authorization, invalid task input, unavailable agents, timeout, execution failure, or failed acceptance checks must produce explicit, auditable outcomes; the system never defaults to pass.
acceptance_criteria: Each enumerated failure mode has a defined outcome state and an explicit record
No failure path continues to the next step or returns success by default
Failure records name the failing stage, matching the ordered-stage failure behaviour required by REQ-P10-11
security_implications: A silent default-to-pass is an unbounded authorization grant

requirements.title: Auditable task status and evidence
requirements.objective: Preserve a complete, auditable task record: task identifiers, ordered plan, selected agent, selection rationale, execution status, verification result, timestamps, and integrity digests - never secrets.
acceptance_criteria: The task record conforms to sps2.p17-task-record/v1
Every state transition is timestamped, and the record carries SHA-256 digests of the plan and of the execution transcripts
Evidence follows .sps/GOVERNANCE.md §4: real captured output, never reconstructed; SKIP and BLOCKED state their reason
A task with no evidence record is at best IMPLEMENTED, never VERIFIED (three-axis rule, .sps/GOVERNANCE.md §1)
security_implications: Undigested, untimestamped records are how an audited artifact diverges from the shipped one

requirements.title: Failure handling and recovery
requirements.objective: Handle execution failures with bounded retry, explicit failure records, and resume from project-local state without corrupting other tasks.
acceptance_criteria: A failed task may be retried only within a recorded bound, and retries are visible in the task record
Task state is persisted to project-local state so an interrupted run resumes without re-executing completed steps
Failure of one task never alters the records of other tasks
security_implications: Unbounded retry is a denial-of-service vector against the user's own machine and provider quotas

requirements.title: Standard-library-only initial implementation
requirements.objective: Implement the initial Task Runner in the Python standard library only; introduce no third-party dependency.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation imports only standard-library and intra-repository modules, machine-checked by the project isolation validator
No dependency installation occurs, and the standing stack constraint is not weakened
security_implications: The stdlib-only policy removes the third-party supply-chain surface entirely

requirements.title: No premature autonomy
requirements.objective: Grant no unrestricted command execution, no automatic deployment, and no bypass of existing approval gates; autonomy is bounded by the explicit allowlist and the gate structure.
acceptance_criteria: Only executables in the explicit authorized allowlist may be invoked, and the allowlist is data, not code paths
No automatic deployment or publish action exists in the initial implementation
Removing or bypassing a gate is a negative-tested violation, not a configuration option
security_implications: Premature autonomy is how an orchestrator becomes an unreviewed actor on the user's machine

requirements.title: Provider compliance
requirements.objective: Use only authorized providers and supported API/CLI access; do not circumvent provider limits, account restrictions, or terms, and do not introduce automatic account rotation intended to bypass quotas.
acceptance_criteria: The execution contract names the authorized provider access mode (the user's own CLI sessions and accounts) and records it in the task record
No account rotation, credential sharing, or quota-circumvention mechanism exists anywhere in the implementation
Provider-side limits are respected; hitting a limit is an explicit auditable outcome (BLOCKED), never a trigger for evasion
security_implications: Quota circumvention violates the terms under which the authorized access exists and would revoke it

execution_security_contract.binding_on: The first Task Runner implementation and every execution it performs. Adoption is recorded as D-P17-2 in sps2/decisions/P17-DECISIONS.json.
execution_security_contract.note: Each boundary below lists its rule, the requirement that implements it, the acceptance criteria, and the evidence required to demonstrate compliance. JSON Schema cannot enforce any of these at record level; they are runtime obligations verified by the negative security suite before GATE-P17-2 can pass.

boundaries.title: Local-only execution
boundaries.rule: No public server, no public network exposure, and no deployment. The harness opens no listening socket and makes no network request of its own; it only spawns the authorized local CLI.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation contains no socket binding and no outbound network call of its own
A negative test asserts the harness fails closed if invoked with any network or deployment flag
boundaries.required_evidence: negative test output; code reference for the absence of network APIs

boundaries.title: Authorized executables
boundaries.rule: Invoke only explicitly authorized CLI tools from an explicit allowlist. Discover availability at runtime by probing. Never assume a tool is available merely because it is documented in the repository.
acceptance_criteria: The allowlist is data, and every invocation resolves against it
Runtime probing determines availability; a documented-but-absent tool is reported unavailable and never selected
A negative test asserts an off-allowlist executable is rejected
boundaries.required_evidence: discovery snapshot in the task record; negative test output

boundaries.title: Provider compliance
boundaries.rule: Do not circumvent provider limits, account restrictions, or terms. Do not introduce automatic account rotation intended to bypass quotas. Use only the user's own authorized CLI sessions and accounts.
acceptance_criteria: The authorized provider access mode is named and recorded per task
No account rotation, credential sharing, or quota-circumvention mechanism exists
Hitting a provider limit yields an explicit BLOCKED outcome
boundaries.required_evidence: task record access-mode field; code reference for the absence of rotation logic

boundaries.title: Process control
boundaries.rule: Every execution must have a bounded timeout, captured stdout/stderr, a recorded exit status, and an auditable execution record.
acceptance_criteria: A timed-out process is terminated and recorded as TIMEOUT
stdout/stderr are captured to transcript files with SHA-256 digests
Exit status is recorded verbatim; non-zero is an explicit outcome
boundaries.required_evidence: execution record with outcome, exit status, and transcript digests; timeout negative test

boundaries.title: Directory confinement
boundaries.rule: Restrict the execution working directory to the authorized project boundary. Define and test the containment mechanism rather than relying on a working-directory setting alone.
acceptance_criteria: Containment is enforced by a defined mechanism, not only by cwd
A negative test attempts to write outside the project boundary and fails closed
boundaries.required_evidence: containment mechanism code reference; confinement negative test output

boundaries.title: Credentials
boundaries.rule: Do not expose API keys, environment secrets, or credentials in task plans, logs, transcripts, or evidence. Do not introduce unrestricted credential access.
acceptance_criteria: No secret value appears in any recorded artefact; secrets are referenced by location only
The execution environment is constructed with an explicit minimal policy
A credential-scrubbing negative test fails when a secret pattern appears in any recorded artefact
boundaries.required_evidence: scrubbing negative test output; environment-construction code reference

boundaries.title: Independent verification
boundaries.rule: Separate execution results from acceptance verification. A successful agent exit code or an agent's own claim is not proof that the task passed.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance is judged by an objective acceptance command or a structurally independent verifier
A task whose acceptance command fails is recorded as failed even when the agent exited 0
The verifier's independence from the executor is stated in the record
boundaries.required_evidence: verification record with independence statement and evidence reference; negative test where agent exits 0 but acceptance fails

boundaries.title: Fail-closed behavior
boundaries.rule: Missing authorization, invalid task input, unavailable agents, timeout, execution failure, or failed acceptance checks must produce explicit, auditable outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Each enumerated failure mode has a defined outcome state and record
No failure path defaults to pass or continues silently
boundaries.required_evidence: one negative test per enumerated failure mode

boundaries.title: No dependency installation
boundaries.rule: Use the Python standard library only for the initial implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Imports are standard-library and intra-repository only, machine-checked by the isolation validator
No dependency installation occurs
boundaries.required_evidence: isolation validator output over the P17 surface

boundaries.title: No premature autonomy
boundaries.rule: Do not add unrestricted command execution, automatic public deployment, or bypasses around existing approval gates.
acceptance_criteria: Only allowlist executables are invocable
No automatic deployment or publish action exists
Gate removal or bypass is a negative-tested violation
boundaries.required_evidence: negative test output for allowlist enforcement and gate bypass

boundaries.title: Evidence integrity
boundaries.rule: Define required task identifiers, plan, selected agent, selection rationale, execution status, verification result, timestamps, and appropriate integrity digests. Never record secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Task records conform to sps2.p17-task-record/v1
Plan and transcripts carry SHA-256 digests
No secret value appears in any field of any record
boundaries.required_evidence: schema validation record; digest verification output; scrubbing negative test

approval_gates.note: Three explicit gates separate governance approval from implementation from execution. No gate may be skipped, and no gate may be self-approved by an agent.

GATE-P17-1.title: Governance foundation approval
GATE-P17-1.what_it_approved: Phase establishment (roadmap amendment), the requirements and execution security contract (this document), the decision record (sps2/decisions/P17-DECISIONS.json), and the task-record schema (sps2/schemas/p17-task-record.schema.json)
GATE-P17-1.what_it_did_not_approve: Task Runner implementation, any execution of an agent CLI, any real task, deployment, network exposure, dependency installation

GATE-P17-2.title: Security review and implementation-plan approval
GATE-P17-2.scope_of_approval: Implementation of Slice 1 within the exact boundaries of the approved revised plan. This approval does NOT authorize real-agent execution (GATE-P17-4 remains OPEN), does NOT satisfy GATE-P17-3, and does NOT mark any Slice 1 component implemented, verified, or approved as an outcome.
requirements: The Task Runner implementation plan is written and presented (plan-gate convention: zero code before approval)
The negative security suite for SEC-P17-01 through SEC-P17-11 is defined
A security review of the implementation against the execution security contract is performed
Explicit User approval of the implementation plan
GATE-P17-2.evidence_required: implementation plan, negative suite definition, security review record, explicit User approval

GATE-P17-3.title: Per-task execution approval
GATE-P17-3.required_before: The first real task execution, and every HIGH or CRITICAL task thereafter
requirements: The specific task, its ordered plan, and its acceptance command are presented
Explicit User approval of that specific task execution (approval-packet convention)
GATE-P17-3.evidence_required: approval record in the task record (approval.state = APPROVED, decided_by_role = USER)

unresolved_questions.question: What is the authoritative initial membership of the authorized agent allowlist?
unresolved_questions.context: Runtime probing in this environment observes the claude, opencode, and copilot CLIs present on PATH, but observation of availability is not authorization: the authoritative allowlist is a security decision, not an engineering default. REQ-P17-03/SEC-P17-02 define the mechanism; the membership must be fixed explicitly.
options: The three observed CLIs (claude, opencode, copilot)
A single CLI for the first slice, extended by later User decision
Allowlist fixed per task by the User at GATE-P17-3
unresolved_questions.decision: Initial authoritative allowlist is exactly ["opencode"] (D-P17-4). Production-purpose allowlist entries are neither probed nor invoked while GATE-P17-4 is OPEN.

unresolved_questions.question: What may verify agent work for HIGH or CRITICAL tasks?
unresolved_questions.context: P12 (planned) forbids agent self-sign-off for HIGH/CRITICAL work. Whether an independent second agent may verify, or only objective acceptance commands may judge, is unresolved and changes the verification verifier enum usage in the task record.
options: Objective commands plus an independent second agent
User review of every HIGH/CRITICAL verification
unresolved_questions.decision: Slice 1 verification is by OBJECTIVE acceptance commands only, executed by a structurally separate verifier whose executable may not be an allowlisted agent (D-P17-5). An independent second agent for HIGH/CRITICAL verification remains a later User decision.

unresolved_questions.question: Does P17 orchestrate multiple concurrent agent processes (parallel specialist lanes) or single-agent execution only?
unresolved_questions.context: skills/sps/SUBAGENT-PLAYBOOK.md defines four parallel lanes at prompt level. Whether the executable backbone runs concurrent agent processes in P17, or starts single-agent and adds fan-out later, is a scope decision with security implications (concurrent subprocess control).
options: Single-agent execution only in P17; fan-out as a later increment
Parallel lanes from the first implementation
unresolved_questions.decision: Slice 1 is single-agent execution only; parallel fan-out is a later increment requiring a new User decision record (D-P17-6).

unresolved_questions.question: How is provider usage and cost observed?
unresolved_questions.context: Provider compliance (SEC-P17-03) requires visibility into usage. Whether usage reporting lives in the task record, a separate project-local log, or is delegated to the provider's own tooling is unresolved.
options: Usage fields in the task record
unresolved_questions.decision: Project-local append-only usage log: agent id, resolved path, probed version, duration, outcome; no provider API calls (D-P17-7).
